blocks.text: The Perfekt commonly reports completed events in conversation. Use a present-tense auxiliary and a past participle. Most verbs take haben; many intransitive verbs expressing a change of location or state take sein. Learn the auxiliary together with the verb.

blocks.de: Wir sind gestern nach Trier gefahren.
blocks.en: We travelled to Trier yesterday.

blocks.de: Ich habe den Bericht gelesen.
blocks.en: I have read the report.

blocks.text: Movement alone is not a universal test: a transitive use such as Ich habe das Auto gefahren takes haben. Separable prefixes precede ge-; inseparable prefixes and -ieren verbs normally have no ge-.
Check: Sie ist um acht angekommen. Ankommen takes sein.

A2.title: Präteritum: sein, haben and modal verbs

blocks.text: Präteritum places an event or state in the past. Sein, haben and modal verbs are especially common in this form even in everyday speech. A modal verb places the other infinitive at the end.

rows: ich war, wir waren / ich hatte, wir hatten

blocks.de: Als Kind konnte ich gut schwimmen.
blocks.en: As a child I could swim well.

blocks.de: Wir hatten keine Zeit und mussten gehen.
blocks.en: We had no time and had to leave.

blocks.text: Past ability konnte is different from hypothetical könnte. The umlaut changes the meaning. A modal verb with another verb normally takes a bare infinitive, not zu.
Put into the past: Ich muss arbeiten.

A verb determines the cases of its objects. With geben, schicken and zeigen, the recipient is normally dative and the thing transferred is accusative. Some verbs, including helfen and danken, take a dative object without an accusative object.

rows: dem Mann / der Frau / dem Kind
den Brief / die Nachricht / das Buch
mir, dir, ihm, ihr / mich, dich, ihn, sie

blocks.de: Ich schicke meiner Schwester einen Brief.
blocks.en: I am sending my sister a letter.

blocks.de: Kannst du mir helfen?
blocks.en: Can you help me?

blocks.text: English word order does not determine German case. With two unstressed personal pronouns, accusative usually precedes dative: Ich gebe es ihr.
Check: Ich danke dem Lehrer. Danken takes dative.

An, auf, hinter, in, neben, über, unter, vor and zwischen can take dative or accusative. Use dative for a location and accusative for a directed change into a spatial relationship. The question is where versus where to, not simply whether movement occurs.

rows: in der Küche / auf dem Tisch
in die Küche / auf den Tisch

blocks.de: Die Kinder laufen im Park.
blocks.en: The children are running in the park.

blocks.de: Sie legt das Buch auf den Tisch.
blocks.en: She puts the book on the table.

blocks.text: Laufen im Park still uses dative because the park is the location of the activity. Do not switch to accusative merely because the verb describes motion.
Complete: Das Bild hängt an ___ Wand.
Check: Das Bild hängt an der Wand. This describes its location.

An adjective before a noun takes an ending showing its grammatical relationship to the noun. After a definite article, -e and -en are the main endings. After ein, the adjective sometimes supplies a gender ending missing from the article. Predicate adjectives do not take these endings.

rows: der gute Film / die gute Idee / das gute Buch
ein guter Film / eine gute Idee / ein gutes Buch
mit dem guten Film / mit einem guten Film

blocks.de: Ich kaufe einen neuen Mantel.
blocks.en: I am buying a new coat.

blocks.de: Der Mantel ist neu.
blocks.en: The coat is new.

blocks.text: The masculine accusative is einen neuen Mantel. Do not add an adjective ending after sein in a simple predicate such as ist neu.
Complete: Das ist ein interessant___ Buch.
Check: Das ist ein interessantes Buch. Buch is neuter nominative.

Use the comparative to compare two things and the superlative for the highest degree in a group. Many short adjectives have an umlaut; several common forms are irregular. A comparative before a noun also needs an adjective ending.

rows: gut - besser - am besten; viel - mehr - am meisten

blocks.de: Dieser Weg ist kürzer als der andere.
blocks.en: This route is shorter than the other one.

blocks.de: Von allen läuft sie am schnellsten.
blocks.en: Of everyone, she runs the fastest.

blocks.text: Use als for inequality and so ... wie for equality. Am besten is predicative/adverbial; before a noun use an inflected form such as der beste Weg.
Complete: Mein Zimmer ist so groß ___ deins.
Check: Mein Zimmer ist so groß wie deins.

A2.title: Reasons and content: weil and dass

blocks.text: Weil introduces a reason; dass introduces reported or thought content. In standard written subordinate clauses, the finite verb goes at the end. A preceding subordinate clause counts as the first unit of the following main clause.

rows: Weil es regnet, bleiben wir zu Hause.

blocks.de: Ich bleibe zu Hause, weil ich krank bin.
blocks.en: I am staying at home because I am ill.

blocks.de: Ich glaube, dass der Zug pünktlich ist.
blocks.en: I think that the train is on time.

blocks.text: Do not keep ordinary main-clause order after weil or dass in standard writing. Separate the subordinate clause with a comma.
Join with weil: Ich bin müde. Ich habe wenig geschlafen.
Check: Ich bin müde, weil ich wenig geschlafen habe.

Use als for a single past occasion or a past period viewed as one situation. Use wenn for repeated events and for present/future conditions or occasions. Both introduce verb-final subordinate clauses.

rows: immer wenn ich zu Besuch kam

blocks.de: Als ich acht war, lebte ich in Bonn.
blocks.en: When I was eight, I lived in Bonn.

blocks.de: Wenn es regnet, nehme ich den Bus.
blocks.en: When it rains, I take the bus.

blocks.text: Als can describe a long period, not only a brief event. For an indirect question asking when, use wann: Ich weiß nicht, wann er kommt.
Choose als or wenn: ___ ich gestern ankam, war es dunkel.
Check: Als ich gestern ankam, war es dunkel.

Some verbs are learned with a reflexive pronoun, such as sich interessieren. With actions directed back at the subject, the pronoun agrees with that subject. If a separate accusative object is present, the reflexive pronoun may be dative.

rows: mich, dich, sich, uns, euch, sich
mir, dir, sich, uns, euch, sich

blocks.de: Ich interessiere mich für Geschichte.
blocks.en: I am interested in history.

blocks.de: Ich wasche mir die Hände.
blocks.en: I am washing my hands.

blocks.text: The pronoun alone does not determine the preposition. Learn sich freuen auf + accusative for anticipation and sich freuen über + accusative for a cause of pleasure.
Check: Du musst dich beeilen. Sich beeilen uses an accusative reflexive pronoun.

After many verbs and adjective expressions, an infinitive clause describes another action. The understood subject is often the main-clause subject. With a separable verb, zu goes between the prefix and the verb stem.

blocks.de: Ich versuche, jeden Tag zu lesen.
blocks.en: I try to read every day.

blocks.de: Es ist wichtig, genug zu schlafen.
blocks.en: It is important to get enough sleep.

blocks.text: Not every verb takes zu. Modal verbs take a bare infinitive. Use a comma for clarity here; certain infinitive groups require it, including those introduced by um, ohne or statt.
Complete: Ich habe vor, morgen früh ___ (aufstehen).
Check: Ich habe vor, morgen früh aufzustehen.

A relative clause adds information about a noun. The relative pronoun takes its gender and number from that noun, but its case comes from its role inside the relative clause. The finite verb is final.

blocks.de: Das ist die Frau, die hier arbeitet.
blocks.en: That is the woman who works here.

blocks.de: Hier ist der Film, den du suchst.
blocks.en: Here is the film you are looking for.

blocks.text: Do not copy the case of the noun in the main clause. In den du suchst, du is the subject and den is the accusative object.
Complete: Das ist der Mann, ___ nebenan wohnt.
Check: Das ist der Mann, der nebenan wohnt. The pronoun is the subject.
Könnte, würde and hätte make requests less direct. Use könnte with a bare infinitive for a polite request about an action. Ich hätte gern requests a thing; ich würde gern expresses a desired action.

blocks.de: Könntest du bitte das Fenster schließen?
blocks.en: Could you please close the window?

blocks.de: Ich hätte gern einen Termin.
blocks.en: I would like an appointment.

blocks.text: These forms do not necessarily refer to past time. Bitte helps with politeness, but word order still follows the normal question pattern.
Make this polite: Helfen Sie mir!

Use the Plusquamperfekt to locate an event before another past reference point. Form it with the Präteritum of haben or sein and the past participle. The choice of auxiliary normally matches the Perfekt.

rows: Nachdem sie angekommen war, rief sie an.

blocks.de: Ich hatte schon gegessen, als er kam.
blocks.en: I had already eaten when he arrived.

blocks.de: Der Zug war abgefahren, bevor wir den Bahnhof erreichten.
blocks.en: The train had departed before we reached the station.

blocks.text: Use a clear past reference point. The form is not simply a more formal replacement for every Perfekt sentence.
Complete: Nachdem ich den Brief ___ (lesen), antwortete ich.
Check: Nachdem ich den Brief gelesen hatte, antwortete ich.
The process passive focuses on an action and what is affected by it. Use werden plus a past participle. An active accusative object can become the passive subject; a dative object remains dative.

blocks.de: Die Straße wird repariert.
blocks.en: The road is being repaired.

blocks.de: Dem Patienten wurde geholfen.
blocks.en: The patient was helped.

blocks.text: The passive Perfekt uses worden, not geworden. Dem Patienten remains dative; passive does not turn every object into nominative.
Change to passive: Die Firma baut eine Brücke.
Check: Eine Brücke wird von der Firma gebaut.
Konjunktiv II presents an imagined or unreal situation. Use wäre, hätte and common modal forms directly; würde + infinitive is useful for many other verbs. A wenn-clause places its finite verb last.

blocks.de: Wenn ich frei hätte, würde ich mitkommen.
blocks.en: If I had time off, I would come along.

blocks.de: An deiner Stelle würde ich nachfragen.
blocks.en: In your position, I would ask for clarification.

blocks.text: Hätte does not automatically mean past time in this construction. For an unreal past event, use hätte/wäre plus a participle.
Complete: Wenn ich du ___, würde ich warten.
Check: Wenn ich du wäre, würde ich warten.

B1.title: Relative clauses with dative and prepositions

blocks.text: A relative pronoun can be dative or follow a preposition. Keep the preposition required by the verb or relationship. The noun being described supplies gender and number; the clause supplies case.

rows: mit dem; auf die; für das
die Frau, mit der ich spreche

blocks.de: Das ist der Kollege, dem ich geholfen habe.
blocks.en: That is the colleague whom I helped.

blocks.de: Die Stadt, in der ich wohne, ist klein.
blocks.en: The town where I live is small.

blocks.text: Plural dative is denen, not den. With people, retain preposition + relative pronoun rather than using a da-compound.
Complete: Das sind die Leute, mit ___ wir reisen.
Check: Das sind die Leute, mit denen wir reisen.
Purpose clauses explain a goal. Um ... zu normally shares its understood subject with the main clause. Damit has an explicit subject and is useful when the people performing the two actions differ.

rows: Ich lerne, um die Prüfung zu bestehen.
Ich helfe dir, damit du fertig wirst.

blocks.de: Sie spart, um ein Fahrrad zu kaufen.
blocks.en: She is saving to buy a bicycle.

blocks.de: Ich spreche langsam, damit alle mich verstehen.
blocks.en: I speak slowly so that everyone understands me.

blocks.text: Damit can also be used when the subjects are the same. Do not use an um-zu clause with a separate finite subject and verb.
Join: Ich öffne die Tür. Die Gäste können hereinkommen.
Check: Ich öffne die Tür, damit die Gäste hereinkommen können.

Obwohl marks a fact that contrasts with the main-clause result. Trotzdem and deshalb are main-clause adverbs: when they come first, the finite verb follows immediately. Deshalb gives a consequence or reason-based conclusion; trotzdem gives an unexpected result.

blocks.de: Obwohl sie müde ist, arbeitet sie weiter.
blocks.en: Although she is tired, she keeps working.

blocks.de: Sie ist müde. Deshalb macht sie eine Pause.
blocks.en: She is tired. Therefore she takes a break.

blocks.text: Obwohl and trotzdem are not interchangeable without changing word order. Avoid Obwohl sie ist müde in standard written German.
Rewrite using trotzdem: Obwohl es kalt ist, geht er schwimmen.
Check: Es ist kalt. Trotzdem geht er schwimmen.

B1.title: Indirect questions: ob and question words

blocks.text: An indirect question is embedded in another sentence. Use ob for a yes/no question and retain a question word such as wann, wo or warum for an information question. Put the finite verb at the end.

blocks.de: Ich weiß nicht, ob er heute kommt.
blocks.en: I do not know whether he is coming today.

blocks.de: Kannst du mir sagen, wo der Bahnhof ist?
blocks.en: Can you tell me where the station is?

blocks.text: Ob means whether here, not a conditional if. Do not preserve the direct question order inside the embedded clause.
Embed: Wann beginnt der Kurs? / Wissen Sie ...
Check: Wissen Sie, wann der Kurs beginnt?

Many verbs select a fixed preposition and case. For things or situations, da-compounds refer back and wo-compounds ask questions. Insert r before a vowel: daran, worauf. For people, use preposition plus a personal or interrogative pronoun.

rows: warten auf + accusative; teilnehmen an + dative
auf ihn warten / auf wen warten?

blocks.de: Worauf wartest du? Ich warte auf den Bus.
blocks.en: What are you waiting for? I am waiting for the bus.

blocks.de: Ich freue mich darauf, dich zu sehen.
blocks.en: I am looking forward to seeing you.

blocks.text: Learn the whole combination, including case. Do not use worauf when you specifically mean which person: Auf wen wartest du?
Replace auf den Termin: Ich warte auf den Termin.

The genitive can link a possessor or associated noun to another noun, especially in writing. Masculine and neuter singular nouns often add -(e)s. Feminine and plural nouns usually do not add a special genitive ending.

blocks.de: Die Farbe des Autos gefällt mir.
blocks.en: I like the colour of the car.

blocks.de: Während des Kurses bleibt das Handy aus.
blocks.en: During the course, the phone stays off.

blocks.text: In everyday speech, von + dative often replaces a possessive genitive. Dative after wegen occurs in speech, but genitive is a useful default for formal writing.

Without an article, an attributive adjective carries much of the case information itself. These are strong endings. Pay particular attention to nominative and accusative plural -e and dative plural -en.

rows: guter Kaffee / kalte Milch / frisches Brot
mit gutem Kaffee / mit kalter Milch / mit frischem Brot

blocks.de: Wir trinken kaltes Wasser.
blocks.en: We are drinking cold water.

blocks.de: Mit frischen Kräutern schmeckt es besser.
blocks.en: It tastes better with fresh herbs.

blocks.text: Dative plural nouns often add -n too: mit frischen Kräutern. Do not add another -n if the plural already ends in -n or -s.
Check: Ich suche frisches Brot. Brot is neuter accusative.
German often uses the present tense with a time expression for future plans. Werden + infinitive can mark a prediction, promise or assumption. The infinitive stays at the end of a main clause.

rows: Er wird jetzt zu Hause sein.

blocks.de: Nächste Woche beginnt mein Kurs.
blocks.en: My course starts next week.

blocks.de: Keine Sorge, ich werde dir helfen.
blocks.en: Do not worry; I will help you.

blocks.text: Werden does not always indicate future time: context can make it an assumption about now. Distinguish werden + infinitive from passive werden + participle.
Form Futur I: Wir besuchen euch.
Paired connectors organise alternatives, additions or exclusions. Connect elements of the same grammatical type. Weder ... noch denies both alternatives; entweder ... oder offers a choice.

blocks.de: Sie spricht sowohl Deutsch als auch Französisch.
blocks.en: She speaks both German and French.

blocks.de: Ich trinke weder Kaffee noch Tee.
blocks.en: I drink neither coffee nor tea.

blocks.text: Do not add nicht to a simple weder ... noch pair. When connecting whole clauses, check the verb position separately in each clause.
Combine with nicht nur ... sondern auch: Der Kurs ist interessant. Er ist praktisch.
Check: Der Kurs ist nicht nur interessant, sondern auch praktisch.

Use hätte or wäre plus a past participle for an imagined alternative to a past event. The auxiliary normally matches the verb's Perfekt auxiliary. Both the condition and the result may refer to the unreal past.

rows: Wenn ich gelernt hätte, hätte ich bestanden.

blocks.de: Wenn ich früher losgegangen wäre, hätte ich den Zug erreicht.
blocks.en: If I had left earlier, I would have caught the train.

blocks.de: Ohne deine Hilfe hätte ich es nicht geschafft.
blocks.en: Without your help, I would not have managed it.

blocks.text: Do not use würde + simple infinitive when you need to mark a completed unreal past event. With a modal verb, the form becomes hätte + infinitive + modal infinitive.
Complete: Wenn sie angerufen ___, wären wir geblieben.
Check: Wenn sie angerufen hätte, wären wir geblieben.

Werden + participle presents a process or event. Sein + participle can present its resulting state. Some sein + participle combinations also behave like ordinary adjective predicates; interpret them in context.

blocks.de: Das Fenster wurde um acht geöffnet.
blocks.en: The window was opened at eight.

blocks.de: Als wir ankamen, war das Fenster geöffnet.
blocks.en: When we arrived, the window was open.

blocks.text: Ist geöffnet and ist geöffnet worden are different: one describes a state, the other a completed opening event. Not all verbs naturally form both constructions.
Choose a state description: Die Rechnung ___ bezahlt.
Check: Die Rechnung ist bezahlt. This presents the paid status, not the payment process.
A modal verb combines with a passive infinitive to express obligation, possibility or permission concerning an action. The passive infinitive consists of the past participle plus werden.

blocks.de: Der Antrag muss bis Freitag eingereicht werden.
blocks.en: The application must be submitted by Friday.

blocks.de: Die Datei konnte nicht geöffnet werden.
blocks.en: The file could not be opened.

blocks.text: Keep werden in the passive infinitive. Muss geprüft is incomplete. Distinguish nicht müssen (no obligation) from nicht dürfen (prohibition).
Rewrite: Man muss die Daten prüfen.

Formal reports often use Konjunktiv I to mark information as someone else's statement. This signals attribution, not automatic disbelief. Common third-person forms end in -e; sein has the distinctive form sei.

rows: er komme / sie habe / es sei
er habe gearbeitet / sie sei angekommen

blocks.de: Die Sprecherin sagt, die Lage sei stabil.
blocks.en: The spokesperson says that the situation is stable.

blocks.de: Er erklärt, er habe die Nachricht nicht erhalten.
blocks.en: He explains that he did not receive the message.

blocks.text: Pronouns and time expressions must suit the reporting perspective. German does not mechanically shift every reported present tense into a past tense.
Report formally: Sie sagt: Ich bin bereit.

Modal verbs can express an assessment of likelihood rather than ability or obligation. Muss can convey a strong inference, dürfte a likely assumption, and könnte a possibility. The strength depends on context and is not an exact probability percentage.

blocks.de: Das Licht ist aus. Sie muss schon schlafen.
blocks.en: The light is off. She must already be asleep.

blocks.de: Der Schlüssel könnte im Büro liegen.
blocks.en: The key might be in the office.

blocks.text: Dürfte in this use is an assumption, not simply past permission. Er muss nicht kommen usually means he does not have to come, not that his arrival is impossible.
Express a possibility: Vielleicht ist der Laden geschlossen.

Partizip I usually presents an ongoing or characteristic active situation. Partizip II often presents a completed or passive/resulting situation, depending on the verb. Before a noun, both take adjective endings.

blocks.de: Die wartenden Fahrgäste wurden informiert.
blocks.en: The waiting passengers were informed.

blocks.de: Wir prüfen die gestern eingegangenen Anträge.
blocks.en: We are checking the applications received yesterday.

blocks.text: Partizip II is not always passive: angekommen describes guests who arrived. Keep modifiers before the participle when building an attributive phrase.
Shorten: die Menschen, die hier arbeiten

Nominalisation turns an event into a noun phrase. It is common in reports and headings, but a verb-based sentence often makes the actor clearer. Preserve the original meaning and do not assume every verb forms a natural noun with -ung.

rows: nachdem geprüft wurde - nach der Prüfung

blocks.de: Nach der Prüfung der Daten erstellen wir den Bericht.
blocks.en: After checking the data, we prepare the report.

blocks.de: Nachdem wir die Daten geprüft haben, erstellen wir den Bericht.
blocks.en: After we have checked the data, we prepare the report.

blocks.text: A noun phrase can hide who performs an action. Use a genitive, von-phrase or full clause when the actor matters.
Rewrite verbally: Vor der Abfahrt kontrolliert sie die Tickets.
Check: Bevor sie abfährt, kontrolliert sie die Tickets.

B2.title: Concessive conditions: selbst wenn and auch wenn

blocks.text: A concessive conditional says that the result holds even under an unfavourable or unexpected condition. Selbst wenn often strengthens the hypothetical meaning. Auch wenn may be conditional or acknowledge a fact; context distinguishes the readings.

rows: Auch wenn ich wenig Zeit habe, ...

blocks.de: Selbst wenn der Zug ausfällt, kommen wir rechtzeitig an.
blocks.en: Even if the train is cancelled, we will arrive on time.

blocks.de: Auch wenn die Aufgabe schwer ist, gebe ich nicht auf.
blocks.en: Even though / even if the task is difficult, I will not give up.

blocks.text: Obwohl normally presents the subordinate statement as a fact. Selbst wenn need not assert that the condition actually holds.
Express even if: Wenn der Preis steigt, kaufen wir es trotzdem.
Check: Selbst wenn der Preis steigt, kaufen wir es.

B2.title: Time relationships: bevor, nachdem, während, seitdem

blocks.text: Temporal connectors specify the relationship between events. Bevor places the main event first, nachdem places the subordinate event first, and während presents overlap. Seitdem describes a starting point for a continuing situation.

blocks.de: Nachdem wir gegessen hatten, gingen wir spazieren.
blocks.en: After we had eaten, we went for a walk.

blocks.de: Seitdem sie hier wohnt, fährt sie mit dem Rad zur Arbeit.
blocks.en: Since she started living here, she has cycled to work.

blocks.text: German commonly uses the present for a situation continuing until now. Do not copy the English present perfect automatically into a seitdem clause or its main clause.
Join with während: Ich koche. Du deckst den Tisch.
Check: Während ich koche, deckst du den Tisch.
Indem describes a means or method. Dadurch, dass links a result to the situation that produces it. Sodass introduces a consequence rather than an intended goal; use damit or um ... zu for purpose.

blocks.de: Sie verbessert ihre Aussprache, indem sie laut liest.
blocks.en: She improves her pronunciation by reading aloud.

blocks.de: Der Zug fiel aus, sodass wir später ankamen.
blocks.en: The train was cancelled, so we arrived later.

blocks.text: Indem does not mean while in the purely temporal sense. A consequence with sodass need not be intended.
Join as a result: Es war sehr laut. Wir konnten nichts verstehen.
Check: Es war sehr laut, sodass wir nichts verstehen konnten.
Weak masculine nouns typically add -(e)n outside nominative singular. Nominalised adjectives, in contrast, retain adjective endings even though they are capitalised and used as nouns.

blocks.de: Ich spreche mit einem Kollegen.
blocks.en: I am speaking with a colleague.

blocks.de: Eine Angestellte hat uns geholfen.
blocks.en: A female employee helped us.

blocks.text: Not every masculine noun is weak. Der Name has mixed forms, including des Namens. Treat nominalised adjectives according to their article and case.

B2.title: Infinitive constructions with lassen, brauchen and scheinen

blocks.text: Lassen commonly takes a bare infinitive and can mean allow or have something done. Negated brauchen with zu expresses lack of necessity in standard written usage. Scheinen + zu expresses an appearance or impression.

blocks.de: Ich lasse mein Fahrrad reparieren.
blocks.en: I am having my bicycle repaired.

blocks.de: Du brauchst heute nicht zu kommen.
blocks.en: You do not need to come today.

blocks.text: Ich lasse das Fahrrad reparieren does not mean that I repair it myself. Do not use zu after lassen in this construction.
Rewrite using scheinen: Es sieht so aus, als wäre er müde.

When a Konjunktiv I form looks identical to the indicative, formal reports often use Konjunktiv II to make the reported status clear. A würde-form is available when a simple form is ambiguous or unsuitable. Context still determines whether a form is reported or hypothetical.

blocks.de: Die Forschenden erklären, sie hätten neue Daten.
blocks.en: The researchers explain that they have new data.

blocks.de: Er sagte, er sei bereits angekommen.
blocks.en: He said that he had already arrived.

blocks.text: Hätten in a report need not mean that the speaker considers the statement false. Do not force a replacement when a clear Konjunktiv I form already fits.
Report clearly: Die Kinder sagen: Wir haben Hunger.
Check: Die Kinder sagen, sie hätten Hunger.

A modal plus a perfect infinitive assesses or reports an earlier event. Müssen/können/könnten can express deductions or possibilities. Sollen attributes a claim to another source; wollen can attribute a claim to the grammatical subject.

blocks.de: Sie muss den Brief schon gelesen haben.
blocks.en: She must already have read the letter.

blocks.de: Er will von dem Fehler nichts gewusst haben.
blocks.en: He claims not to have known about the mistake.

blocks.text: Er soll gegangen sein reports what others say; er will gegangen sein reports his own claim in the relevant reading. Neither construction by itself proves the claim true.
Express a past possibility: Vielleicht hat sie den Bus verpasst.
Check: Sie könnte den Bus verpasst haben.

Several constructions present an action without naming its performer. Sich lassen + infinitive often expresses possibility. Sein + zu-infinitive may express necessity or possibility, depending on context. An adjective in -bar can express suitability or possibility where the word exists.

blocks.de: Das Problem lässt sich leicht lösen.
blocks.en: The problem can be solved easily.

blocks.de: Die Unterlagen sind bis Montag einzureichen.
blocks.en: The documents must be submitted by Monday.

blocks.text: Sein + zu is not always obligation: Das ist kaum zu verstehen expresses difficulty/possibility. Not every verb has a natural -bar adjective.
Rewrite with sich lassen: Man kann die Tür öffnen.

A participial attribute can condense a relative clause into a noun phrase. Place the participle after its complements and before the noun, then give it the required adjective ending. This is frequent in formal writing but becomes difficult to read when overloaded.

rows: die Daten, die gestern erhoben wurden

blocks.de: Die von der Behörde veröffentlichten Zahlen sind vorläufig.
blocks.en: The figures published by the authority are provisional.

blocks.de: Wir befragen die seit Jahren hier lebenden Menschen.
blocks.en: We interview the people who have been living here for years.

blocks.text: Keep the time and voice interpretation appropriate to the verb. Use a relative clause if several modifiers make the noun phrase hard to follow.
Expand: die im Ausland erworbenen Kenntnisse
Check: die Kenntnisse, die im Ausland erworben wurden

Formal German often expresses an action through a noun plus a relatively general verb. Learn the whole combination with its article and preposition. Some pairs distinguish an active cause from a resulting state.

rows: zur Anwendung kommen / etwas zur Anwendung bringen

blocks.de: Der Ausschuss trifft morgen eine Entscheidung.
blocks.en: The committee will make a decision tomorrow.

blocks.de: Die neue Regelung kommt ab Mai zur Anwendung.
blocks.en: The new regulation will be applied from May.

blocks.text: These are conventional combinations, not freely interchangeable nouns and verbs. A simpler verb such as entscheiden is often clearer when no special nuance is needed.
Rewrite with a verb: Wir treffen eine Entscheidung.

Advanced connectors distinguish conditions, restrictions and alternatives. Sofern means provided that, es sei denn introduces an exception, and zumal introduces an additional reason that strengthens the argument.

blocks.de: Wir stimmen zu, sofern die Kosten begrenzt bleiben.
blocks.en: We agree, provided that the costs remain limited.

blocks.de: Ich komme, es sei denn, ich muss arbeiten.
blocks.en: I will come unless I have to work.

blocks.text: After es sei denn, a clause without dass normally has main-clause order. After sofern and zumal, use subordinate verb-final order.
Add a condition with sofern: Wir liefern. Die Ware ist verfügbar.
Check: Wir liefern, sofern die Ware verfügbar ist.

German word order helps distinguish a topic from new or contrastive information. One constituent normally occupies the position before the finite verb in a declarative main clause. Short known pronouns tend to come early; longer or new information often comes later.

rows: Ich habe ihr das Buch gegeben.
Das Buch habe ich ihr gegeben.
Gestern habe ich ihr das Buch gegeben.

blocks.de: Den Bericht habe ich schon gelesen.
blocks.en: I have already read the report.

blocks.de: Ihr habe ich das Buch gegeben, nicht ihm.
blocks.en: I gave the book to her, not to him.

blocks.text: The first position is one constituent, not necessarily one word. Standard patterns such as time-cause-manner-place are useful tendencies, not rules that override context and emphasis.
Front gestern: Ich habe gestern den Bericht geschrieben.
Check: Gestern habe ich den Bericht geschrieben. The finite verb stays second.

C1.title: Focus particles and the scope of negation

blocks.text: Focus particles such as nur, auch and sogar associate with a focused element. Their position and spoken stress affect interpretation. Negation likewise has scope: denying an entire proposition differs from contrasting one constituent.

rows: Nur Anna hat den Bericht gelesen.
Anna hat nur den Bericht gelesen.

blocks.de: Sogar Paul hat die Aufgabe gelöst.
blocks.en: Even Paul solved the task.

blocks.de: Ich habe nicht den Bericht kritisiert, sondern die Methode.
blocks.en: I criticised not the report but the method.

blocks.text: Written position alone may not settle every possible reading; intonation and context also matter. Place the particle near the intended focus when clarity matters.
Express that Anna read the report and nothing else.
Check: Anna hat nur den Bericht gelesen.

In compound past forms, a modal verb governing another infinitive normally appears as an infinitive instead of a participle. With this cluster in a subordinate clause, finite haben normally precedes the infinitives.

blocks.de: Ich habe gestern länger bleiben müssen.
blocks.en: I had to stay longer yesterday.

blocks.de: Er sagt, dass er nicht hat kommen können.
blocks.en: He says that he was unable to come.

blocks.text: Do not write hat arbeiten gemusst in this construction. Without another infinitive, a modal can have an ordinary participle, as in Das habe ich nicht gewollt.
Put in Perfekt: Sie muss warten.

Als ob introduces an unreal or distanced comparison with verb-final order. A comparison with als alone places the finite verb immediately after als. Wishes can use wenn with doch or nur, or an initial Konjunktiv II verb.

blocks.de: Sie tut so, als ob sie nichts gehört hätte.
blocks.en: She acts as if she had heard nothing.

blocks.de: Wäre ich nur früher losgefahren!
blocks.en: If only I had set off earlier!

blocks.text: Present comparison and earlier event require different forms: wüsste versus gehört hätte. Avoid treating all Konjunktiv II clauses as past tense.
Rewrite without ob: Er spricht, als ob er der Chef wäre.
Check: Er spricht, als wäre er der Chef.
A correlate anticipates or refers to a clause and fulfils a role required by the main construction. Es may anticipate a subject or object clause; a da-compound retains a verb's required preposition.

rows: Es freut mich, dass du kommst.

blocks.de: Ich rechne damit, dass der Zug verspätet ist.
blocks.en: I expect the train to be late.

blocks.de: Es ist unklar, ob der Plan funktioniert.
blocks.en: It is unclear whether the plan will work.

blocks.text: Do not drop a required preposition merely because its complement is a clause. Whether a correlate is optional depends on the verb and construction.
Complete: Ich freue mich ___, dass du kommst.
Check: Ich freue mich darüber, dass du kommst.

Dessen and deren connect possession or association within a relative clause. Their form depends on the antecedent: dessen for masculine/neuter singular and deren for feminine singular or plural. The possessed noun still has its own role in the clause.

blocks.de: Die Autorin, deren Buch ich lese, kommt morgen.
blocks.en: The author whose book I am reading is coming tomorrow.

blocks.de: Das ist der Mann, mit dessen Tochter ich arbeite.
blocks.en: That is the man whose daughter I work with.

blocks.text: Dessen does not change to agree with Tochter. The preposition mit governs the case of the larger phrase mit dessen Tochter.
Complete: die Kinder, ___ Eltern hier wohnen
Check: die Kinder, deren Eltern hier wohnen

C2.title: Reported discourse: attribution across a paragraph

blocks.text: In extended reporting, a reporting frame can govern several following sentences. Consistent Konjunktiv helps readers distinguish the source's account from the writer's own assertion. Reintroduce the source when the perspective would otherwise become unclear.

rows: Die Lage sei stabil. Es gebe keine Gefahr.
Unabhängige Daten liegen noch nicht vor.

blocks.de: Die Firma erklärte, die Anlage sei sicher. Alle Prüfungen seien abgeschlossen.
blocks.en: The company stated that the facility was safe. All inspections had been completed, it said.

blocks.de: Ob diese Angaben zutreffen, ist noch unklar.
blocks.en: Whether this information is correct remains unclear.

blocks.text: Konjunktiv marks reporting but does not identify a source by itself. A switch to indicative may change the perceived voice; make that shift explicit in sensitive factual writing.
Add a second reported sentence: Der Sprecher erklärte, es gebe keine Verzögerung. Alle Termine ...
Check: Alle Termine würden eingehalten. The replacement form keeps the statement within the reported account.

A counterfactual condition and its consequence need not refer to the same time. A past action can have an imagined present consequence. Use explicit time expressions to make each reference point clear instead of mechanically copying the same tense into both clauses.

rows: Wenn ich nicht so vergesslich wäre, hätte ich gestern angerufen.

blocks.de: Wenn sie früher gespart hätte, hätte sie heute weniger Sorgen.
blocks.en: If she had saved earlier, she would have fewer worries today.

blocks.de: Hätten wir den Zug genommen, wären wir jetzt schon dort.
blocks.en: If we had taken the train, we would already be there now.

blocks.text: Hätte can be an auxiliary marking an unreal past or a lexical verb meaning would have in the present. Identify the full verb phrase and time adverbials.
Complete: Wenn ich gestern früher eingeschlafen wäre, ___ ich jetzt nicht so müde.
Check: Wenn ich gestern früher eingeschlafen wäre, wäre ich jetzt nicht so müde.

Formal and literary German can express concession through an initial verb or through a wh-expression plus auch/immer. These patterns present the main claim as valid regardless of the concession. They require attention to clause structure and register.

blocks.de: So überzeugend die Erklärung auch klingt, sie beantwortet nicht alle Fragen.
blocks.en: However convincing the explanation sounds, it does not answer every question.

blocks.de: Was immer geschieht, wir halten zusammen.
blocks.en: Whatever happens, we will stick together.

blocks.text: These constructions can sound formal or emphatic. In So schwierig es auch ist, the verb is final; do not imitate a main clause after the opening adjective.
Reformulate: Auch wenn es sehr teuer ist, wir brauchen es.
Check: So teuer es auch ist, wir brauchen es.

Modal particles such as doch, ja, eben and wohl can signal assumptions, expectations or a stance toward the listener. They are often unstressed and cannot be translated with one fixed English word. Distinguish this use from stressed adverbs or connectors with the same spelling.

blocks.de: Du hast doch morgen frei, oder?
blocks.en: You have tomorrow off, don't you?

blocks.de: Dann müssen wir eben warten.
blocks.en: Then we will just have to wait.

blocks.text: Tone and context can change the effect from friendly to impatient. Avoid inserting particles mechanically into formal reports or assuming doch always means but.
What does ja contribute in Das ist ja interessant!?
Check: It can mark a newly noticed, surprising fact here. The effect is contextual; it is not a yes answer.

The scope of a quantifier or negation affects the claim being made. Nicht alle denies that every member satisfies a condition; keiner excludes every member. Contrastive phrasing and explicit reformulation help prevent a stronger claim than the evidence supports.

blocks.de: Nicht jeder Fehler führt zu einem Ausfall.
blocks.en: Not every error leads to a failure.

blocks.de: Keiner der Vorschläge wurde angenommen.
blocks.en: None of the proposals was accepted.

blocks.text: Nicht alle does not by itself guarantee that some were accepted; it only rules out all being accepted. Avoid treating nicht müssen as a straightforward impossibility claim.
Do these mean the same: Nicht alle kamen. / Niemand kam.?
Check: No. Niemand kam says nobody came. Nicht alle kamen only says that the full group did not come.

C2.title: Long noun phrases: attachment and ambiguity

blocks.text: In dense formal noun phrases, several genitives, prepositional phrases and participles can compete for attachment. Identify the head noun first, then decide which modifier belongs to which noun. Where two readings remain possible, rewriting is better than guessing.

rows: die von der Ärztin durchgeführte Untersuchung
die Untersuchung, bei der die Ärztin untersucht wurde

blocks.de: Die Untersuchung der Ärztin dauerte eine Stunde.
blocks.en: The doctor's examination / the examination of the doctor lasted an hour.

blocks.de: Die Ärztin führte die Untersuchung innerhalb einer Stunde durch.
blocks.en: The doctor carried out the examination within an hour.

blocks.text: A genitive does not always identify an owner. With action nouns it may identify the actor or the affected participant. Context may help, but the form alone can remain ambiguous.
Rewrite to make the actor explicit: die Kritik des Ausschusses

C2.title: Relative clauses referring to a whole proposition

blocks.text: A relative continuation can refer to the preceding situation as a whole rather than to a single noun. Was is common for this function. Wo-compounds preserve a required preposition when referring back to a fact or event.

blocks.de: Der Zug kam pünktlich, was uns überraschte.
blocks.en: The train arrived on time, which surprised us.

blocks.de: Sie sagte sofort zu, womit ich nicht gerechnet hatte.
blocks.en: She agreed immediately, which I had not expected.

blocks.text: Was here refers to the preceding fact, not necessarily to the nearest noun. If the reference could be unclear, use a new sentence with Diese Entscheidung or Dieser Umstand.
Join with worüber: Sie hat bestanden. Ich freue mich darüber.
Check: Sie hat bestanden, worüber ich mich freue.

Coordinated clauses can omit material recoverable from the other clause. Parallel structure makes the omitted words easy to reconstruct. In careful writing, avoid ellipsis when it hides a change in grammatical role, agreement or meaning.

rows: Anna liest den Bericht, Paul die Anlage.
Sie öffnete die Datei und prüfte die Zahlen.

blocks.de: Die erste Gruppe arbeitet morgens, die zweite abends.
blocks.en: The first group works in the morning, the second in the evening.

blocks.de: Er hat den Text gelesen und die Fehler markiert.
blocks.en: He has read the text and marked the errors.

blocks.text: An omitted element must be recoverable, not merely imaginable. Keep coordinated structures grammatically compatible; repeat the full clause if a shared word would need a different form.
Restore the omitted verb: Maria bestellte Tee, Jonas Kaffee.
Check: Maria bestellte Tee, Jonas bestellte Kaffee.

C2.title: Fronting and the Nachfeld in complex sentences

blocks.text: German can place a long clause after the right part of the verbal bracket, in the Nachfeld. This reduces the load inside the sentence. Fronting, by contrast, establishes a topic or contrast before the finite verb. Use both to control readability.

rows: Sie hat erklärt, warum sie absagt.
Warum sie absagt, hat sie erklärt.
Er hat länger gewartet, als wir erwartet hatten.

blocks.de: Ich habe nicht damit gerechnet, dass so viele Menschen kommen.
blocks.en: I had not expected so many people to come.

blocks.de: Dass der Plan scheitern könnte, hatte niemand bedacht.
blocks.en: Nobody had considered that the plan might fail.

blocks.text: A heavy clause after the bracket is not a licence to put ordinary complements anywhere. Preserve the grammatical relationship and required correlates such as damit.
Front the content clause: Sie hat gesagt, dass sie kommt.
Check: Dass sie kommt, hat sie gesagt.

Legal and administrative writing often compresses conditions into prepositional phrases. Bei can mark a condition; mangels gives absence as a reason; vorbehaltlich marks a reservation. Expand them into clauses when precision or accessibility benefits.

blocks.de: Bei rechtzeitiger Zahlung entfällt die Gebühr.
blocks.en: If payment is made on time, the fee does not apply.

blocks.de: Die Entscheidung gilt vorbehaltlich der Zustimmung des Ausschusses.
blocks.en: The decision is subject to the committee's approval.

blocks.text: These phrases differ in meaning, not just style. Vorbehaltlich signals a reservation rather than an unconditional promise. Keep the genitive after mangels and vorbehaltlich in this formal pattern.
Expand: Bei einer Änderung informieren wir Sie.
Check: Wenn sich etwas ändert, informieren wir Sie.

C2.title: Futur II: completion and retrospective inference

blocks.text: Futur II uses werden plus a perfect infinitive. It can present an action as completed by a future reference point or express an assumption about an earlier event. Time adverbials and the situation distinguish the readings.

rows: Bis morgen wird sie angekommen sein.

blocks.de: Bis Freitag werden wir den Bericht fertiggestellt haben.
blocks.en: By Friday we will have completed the report.

blocks.de: Er wird die Nachricht wohl übersehen haben.
blocks.en: He probably overlooked the message.

blocks.text: The form does not force a future interpretation. For an assumption about a past event, translating mechanically as will have may sound unnatural in English.
Identify the reading: Sie ist nicht da; sie wird schon gegangen sein.
Check: This is an inference about an earlier departure, not a prediction of a future departure.

C2.title: Editing for register, precision and agency

blocks.text: Advanced control means choosing a structure that fits the purpose, not making every sentence longer. Compare passive and active voice, nominal and verbal style, and degrees of commitment. Preserve who did what and how certain the claim is when reformulating.

blocks.de: Die Ergebnisse legen nahe, dass die Maßnahme wirkt.
blocks.en: The results suggest that the measure works.

blocks.de: Die Ergebnisse beweisen, dass die Maßnahme wirkt.
blocks.en: The results prove that the measure works.

blocks.text: The two example verbs make different evidential claims. A stylistic rewrite must not silently turn a possibility into a fact or erase an actor whose responsibility matters.
Make the actor explicit: Nach Prüfung des Antrags erfolgt eine Rückmeldung durch das Team.
Check: Nachdem das Team den Antrag geprüft hat, gibt es eine Rückmeldung. The team remains the actor in both actions.
